title: Specs Tokens Document Schema
description: What each token in a foundation is for, authored as foundations/<concern>/tokens.yaml. A reference table, not a rulebook: useWhen says what each token is for, dontUseWhen says which are off-limits and what replaces them. Neither binds a reader the way a guideline does, which is why this is its own document — a foundation's guidelines.yaml is about how tokens, themes and raw values are applied across the catalogue, and thirty tokens with a sentence each is reference material that was drowning those rules. A token is identified by the path the library spells it with, spaces and capitals included; a DSDS-legal identifier is derived at export (DSPEC-60), never authored here. This file is self-contained. (ADR-118)

dontUseWhen.description: Which tokens are off-limits, why, and what replaces them.

TokensMeta.description: Authorship and review status for the document as a whole. Every member is optional.

concern.description: The foundation this document covers, restating what the containing directory names.

status.description: Where the document sits in its review cycle.

oneOf.description: Drafted and awaiting a ratifier; its descriptions are not yet the system's position.
Reviewed and adopted; its descriptions are the system's position.
Superseded or withdrawn; kept for the record and not to be followed.

author.description: Who authored it. Duplicates git history, and is here for a reader who will not consult git.

updated.description: When it was last revised, as YYYY-MM-DD. Hand-maintained, so it can go stale.

sources.description: The generated reports this document was synthesized from, as workspace-relative paths.

TokenPointer.description: A reference to one thing, either inside this workspace or outside it. Exactly one member is present: to names something the workspace holds, href names something it does not. Resolution of to is DSPEC-57.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace — normally another token's path.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

TokenRef.description: A pointer that states its relationship explicitly, for the relationships that have no field of their own.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

rel.description: What the target is to the token carrying this ref.

oneOf.description: The target describes the same token at another scope, and the duplication is deliberate.
The target is an issue or document bearing on this token, without describing it.
The target is the code or package this token comes from.
The target is the design file or collection this token comes from.
The target is a running example of this token in use.

TokenSubject.description: One token, and what it is for.

$token.description: The token, as a <collection>/<group>/<name> path spelled as the library spells it — the same form every spec's $token and analysis/foundations.yaml carry.

$description.description: What it is for, or why it is off-limits.

alternatives.description: What to reach for instead of this one. Meaningful under dontUseWhen, where its absence says something true: nothing replaces this token.

refs.description: Related references, including same-as when this restates a token at another scope.
